clue.text: Disabled carrier may go to the wall

explanation.surface: Something carrying an invalid could end up shoved against a wall.
explanation.walkthrough: In bricklaying a stretcher is a brick laid lengthwise along the face of a wall, so the second sense is literal building jargon.
explanation.definitionFit: A litter for the sick or injured carries them, and a brick laid with its long side showing is built into a wall.

clue.text: No longer out to end solicitor's career

explanation.surface: Exit from the profession ends a lawyer's working life.
explanation.walkthrough: Strikers are 'out'; when the strike is off they are back at work. A solicitor struck off the roll can no longer practise.
explanation.definitionFit: When industrial action is called off workers stop being out; removal from the roll of solicitors bars one from practising.

clue.text: Some vibration in gear

indicators.note: only some of the word's letters are used, a run inside it

explanation.surface: A little shaking when the car is in gear.
explanation.definitionFit: A gear is a set ratio of turns between engine and wheels, so mechanics call a gear by that term.

clue.text: One who picked off the apple the legend is revealing

parts.words: One who picked off the apple
parts.note: William Tell shot an apple off his son's head with a crossbow
a tale is a legend or story

explanation.surface: The story of the man who shot the apple is quite telling.
explanation.definitionFit: Telltale signs give something away and disclose it.

clue.text: Present heartless song for the passing on of parents

parts.note: here means present, as in a roll call

indicators.note: heartless means one of the central letters of the word for song is removed

parts.note: a ditty is a short simple song

explanation.surface: A gift of a cold song for a parents' funeral.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' drops one of the two middle Ts of DITTY to leave DITY.
explanation.definitionFit: Inheritance of traits from mother and father to child is the transmission of characteristics.

clue.text: Forcibly remove girl with outbreak of spots

indicators.note: with here means the outbreak word has the girl's name set in it

parts.note: a rash is an outbreak of spots on the skin
Vi is a girl's name, short for Violet

explanation.surface: Someone forcibly carries off a girl who has come out in spots.
explanation.definitionFit: To ravish once meant to seize and carry off by force.

clue.text: Hair style pleases the French

explanation.surface: A hairdo that delights the French.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition is a foreign word: the French verb form for 'pleases' is spelt the same as the braid.
explanation.definitionFit: A braid of interwoven strands is a way to dress hair, and in French 'il plaît' means 'it pleases'.

clue.text: The platform for goods (but not passenger) carriage

definitions.text: The platform for goods (but not passenger) carriage

parts.words: The platform for goods (but not passenger) carriage
parts.note: read as a flat portable base on which freight is stacked for moving, not a railway platform

explanation.surface: A station platform serving freight trains but not passenger trains.
explanation.definitionFit: A wooden base on which goods are stacked for lifting by forklift and transport.

clue.text: Like a member of the Monstrous Regiment?

definitions.text: Like a member of the Monstrous Regiment?

parts.words: Like a member of the Monstrous Regiment?
parts.note: John Knox's tract 'The Monstrous Regiment of Women' gave the phrase meaning women; the question asks for a word meaning like a tall strong warrior woman

explanation.surface: Asks what a soldier of some fearsome army is like.
explanation.walkthrough: John Knox's 1558 pamphlet attacked 'the Monstrous Regiment of Women', regiment meaning rule; the phrase became a jocular name for women.
explanation.definitionFit: Like the legendary female warriors of Greek myth: a strong, powerfully built woman.

clue.text: 100 mph American state carriage

parts.note: doing a ton is British slang for driving at 100 mph
GA is the postal abbreviation for Georgia

explanation.surface: A carriage racing at 100 mph across an American state.
explanation.definitionFit: A light two-wheeled horse-drawn vehicle used in India.

clue.text: Snake left for rodent operative to catch

indicators.note: the rat-catching word grabs and holds the letter for left inside itself

parts.note: a ratter is a dog or person employed to kill rats

explanation.surface: A snake left out for the pest controller to trap.
explanation.definitionFit: Rattlesnakes are commonly nicknamed after the warning noise of their tails.

clue.text: Bad character takes half a football team in

parts.note: Aston Villa is an English football club, and Villa is one of the two words of its name
taken as written

explanation.surface: A rogue enlists half of a football side.
explanation.walkthrough: Half a team suggests taking a few letters of ELEVEN, but it means one word of the two-word club name Aston Villa, a Birmingham football club; 'takes' just joins it to IN.
explanation.definitionFit: A wicked character in a story or play is its baddie.

clue.text: Gilbert the Filbert grabs ring and gets severe punishment

indicators.note: the Edwardian dandy word seizes the ring-shaped letter and holds it inside

parts.note: the music-hall song calls Gilbert the Filbert 'the colonel of the Knuts', a knut being an Edwardian dandy
O is ring-shaped

explanation.surface: A music-hall toff snatches a ring and is harshly punished for it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gilbert the Filbert' is a 1914 British music-hall song about a fop, the Knut (a dandy of the day).
explanation.definitionFit: A knout was a Russian whip, and a flogging with it was a brutal penalty.

clue.text: Odd seamen concealed this Shakespearian heroine

indicators.note: the name lies disguised within these letters, needing rearrangement to be uncovered

explanation.surface: Some strange sailors smuggled a Shakespeare heroine aboard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'concealed' looks like a hidden-word signal, but no run of letters spells her; the nine letters of ODD SEAMEN are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Othello's wife, whom he murders out of jealousy, is the tragic heroine of that play.

clue.text: As a floor-covering this might be too chill

indicators.note: these letters might be turned into the word wanted if put in a new order

explanation.surface: Used on the floor, this material might feel too cold.
explanation.definitionFit: A cloth treated with oil to make it waterproof was once laid as a floor or table covering.

clue.text: Defeated agent, native of Oxford

parts.note: lost means defeated
an agent is something that brings about an effect, a cause

explanation.surface: A beaten spy who was born in Oxford.
explanation.walkthrough: Matthew Arnold called Oxford the 'home of lost causes', so such a thing is figuratively native to it.
explanation.definitionFit: Arnold's famous phrase for Oxford makes a hopeless venture something at home there.

clue.text: It's not hard to drag one's feet

explanation.surface: Shuffling along is easy enough.
explanation.definitionFit: Floppy and lacking stiffness is one sense; walking with an uneven, impeded gait is the other.

clue.text: As an afterthought doctor put in an appearance in David's opera

parts.note: PS, postscript, is an afterthought added to a letter

indicators.note: the doctor's letters are put inside the phrase for an appearance

parts.note: a look is an appearance, so 'an appearance' gives A LOOK
MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's qualification

explanation.surface: A doctor turned up at the last minute at a performance of David's opera.
explanation.walkthrough: Opera here is Latin 'works': King David's works are the psalms, collected in this volume.
explanation.definitionFit: A volume of hymns traditionally attributed to King David is his collected works.

clue.text: Things are bought to a halt when he starts flagging

definitions.text: Things are bought to a halt when he starts flagging

parts.words: Things are bought to a halt when he starts flagging
parts.note: read as a match official whose raised flag stops play, not a tired person whose energy flags

explanation.surface: Everything stops when he begins to tire.
explanation.walkthrough: The page prints 'bought' for 'brought'. Flagging suggests tiring, but the official signals offside or out of play by waving a flag.
explanation.definitionFit: The touchline official in football raises his flag to stop play for offside or the ball going out.

clue.text: Dirty, immature girl in tree

indicators.note: in means the shortened girl's name sits inside the tree

parts.note: a birch is a tree

indicators.note: immature means not fully grown, so the name loses its final letter

parts.note: Esme is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A young girl up a tree gets dirty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'immature' cuts the last letter of ESME to give ESM, which goes 'in' BIRCH.
explanation.definitionFit: To besmirch is to soil or sully, literally or a reputation.

clue.text: Join in loud familiarity

parts.note: F, forte, is the musical direction for loud
use, as in being accustomed to something, means habitual familiarity

explanation.surface: Join in, loud and friendly.
explanation.definitionFit: To melt or merge things together unites them.

clue.text: The country represented by Bahrein Island

indicators.note: the letters are presented anew in a different order

explanation.surface: A nation stood for by a Gulf island.
explanation.walkthrough: The page spells the Gulf state the older way, Bahrein, which supplies the E that the modern spelling lacks.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin name for Ireland is a poetic name for that country.

clue.text: The box is showing the "Carry On'" sequence

parts.note: to cart is to carry
taken as written

explanation.surface: Television is showing the Carry On series of comedy films.
explanation.walkthrough: The Carry On films are a long-running series of British comedies; here the title is split into its two words.
explanation.definitionFit: A cardboard container is a box.

clue.text: An Oval trophy for the holder

parts.note: an egg is an oval object
a cup is a trophy

explanation.surface: A trophy won at the Oval cricket ground goes to the holder.
explanation.walkthrough: The Oval is a London cricket ground and trophy holders keep the cup, but here an oval is simply an egg.
explanation.definitionFit: A small cup holds a boiled egg at breakfast.

clue.text: The land of idleness, said to be narcotic

indicators.note: said means the drug's name is spoken, giving a word with a similar sound

parts.note: cocaine is a narcotic drug

explanation.surface: A lazy paradise is rumoured to be a drug.
explanation.definitionFit: In medieval legend, a mythical country of luxury and sloth where food is free.

clue.text: Stupid clown, originally royal fool

indicators.note: originally means only the start of the word is used

parts.note: R stands for royal, as in RN
an ass is a fool

explanation.surface: A dim jester, once the king's fool.
explanation.definitionFit: Crass means grossly dense or insensitive.

clue.text: Form of address in musical demand

explanation.surface: A way of addressing someone is much requested in shows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Call Me Madam' is an Irving Berlin musical; its title is a demand to be addressed in this way.
explanation.definitionFit: A polite way of addressing a woman, and the word the Irving Berlin show title demands to be called.

clue.text: The cloth suspended — padre in error?

indicators.note: in error means the letters are wrongly placed and need reordering

explanation.surface: The priest hung up — was he wrong?
explanation.definitionFit: A hanging curtain or fabric.

clue.text: Wet kind of sport — polo, maybe?

definitions.text: Wet kind of sport — polo, maybe?

parts.words: Wet kind of sport — polo, maybe?
parts.note: polo played in the water by swimmers is an example of a sport carried on in a pool

explanation.surface: A soggy sport such as polo, perhaps.
explanation.definitionFit: Relating to water, as water polo is a game played in a pool.

clue.text: Virgil about managed to be a Christian convert

indicators.note: the poet's surname goes round the other piece

parts.note: Publius Vergilius Maro was Virgil's full name
ran, as in ran a business, means managed

explanation.surface: The Roman poet reportedly managed to become a Christian.
explanation.definitionFit: Spanish and Portuguese Jews forced to convert to Christianity in the Middle Ages were given this name.

clue.text: Rudolf, without any doubt, is a big mug

indicators.note: without means the letters of hesitation are left out

parts.note: Rudolf Steiner was the Austrian founder of anthroposophy and Steiner schools
er is the sound of hesitation or doubt

explanation.surface: Rudolf is undoubtedly a big idiot.
explanation.definitionFit: A large beer tankard is a kind of mug.

clue.text: To economize, make a gesture and get imitation gold

parts.note: to pinch is to scrimp or economize
to beck is to beckon, making a gesture

explanation.surface: To save money, signal and buy fake gold.
explanation.definitionFit: An alloy of copper and zinc used in cheap jewellery to look like gold.
